title: A refactor moving exports to a new RealmExport model dropped the realm filter on deletion, so an admin of one organization could delete another organization's export.

findings.explanation: The PR changes delete_realm_export to fetch the RealmExport row by user-controlled id only: `RealmExport.objects.get(id=export_id)`. The base version scoped the lookup to the caller's realm (`RealmAuditLog.objects.get(id=export_id, realm=user.realm, ...)`). The new RealmExport model has a `realm` FK (realms.py:1319), but the PR never filters by `user.realm`. A realm admin in one organization can therefore delete (and the action deletes the tarball for) a RealmExport belonging to a different organization by guessing/enumerating the integer id — a cross-realm IDOR. The @require_realm_admin decorator only enforces the admin role, not ownership of the specific export row.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the lookup to the caller's realm, e.g. `RealmExport.objects.get(id=export_id, realm=user.realm)`, so a realm admin can only delete exports belonging to their own organization.
